==Problem==

All the numbers <imath>1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9</imath> are written in a <imath>3\times3</imath> array of squares, one number in each square, in such a way that if two numbers are consecutive then they occupy squares that share an edge. The numbers in the four corners add up to <imath>18</imath>. What is the number in the center?

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 5\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ 6\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ 7\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ 8\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ 9</imath>

==Solution 1==
Consecutive numbers share an edge. That means that it is possible to walk from <imath>1</imath> to <imath>9</imath> by single steps north, south, east, or west. Consequently, the squares in the diagram with different shades have different parity:<asy>size(4cm);
for(int i=0;i<3;++i)for(int j=0;j<3;++j)filldraw(box((i,j),(i+1,j+1)),gray((i+j)%2*.2+.7));</asy>
But since there are only four even numbers in the set, the five darker squares must contain the odd numbers, which sum to <imath>1+3+5+7+9=25.</imath> Therefore if the sum of the numbers in the corners is <imath>18</imath>, the number in the center must be <imath>\boxed {\textbf{(C) }7}</imath>.

==Solution 2 - Trial and Error==
Quick testing shows that
<cmath>3~2~1</cmath>
<cmath>4~7~8</cmath>
<cmath>5~6~9</cmath>
is a valid solution. <imath>3+1+5+9 = 18</imath>, and the numbers follow the given condition. The center number is found to be <imath>\boxed {\textbf{(C) }7}</imath>.. [[User:Adihaya|— @adihaya]] ([[User talk:Adihaya|talk]]) 12:27, 21 February 2016 (EST) ~edited

==Solution 3 (not rigorous)==
First let the numbers be
<cmath>1   ~8~   7 </cmath>
<cmath>2  ~ 9   ~6</cmath>
<cmath>3  ~ 4~   5</cmath>
with the numbers <imath>1-8</imath> around the outsides and <imath>9</imath> in the middle. We see that the sum of the four corner numbers is <imath>16</imath>. If we switch <imath>7</imath> and <imath>9</imath>, then the corner numbers will add up to <imath>18</imath> and the consecutive numbers will still be touching each other. The answer is <imath>\boxed {\textbf{(C) }7}</imath>. ~edited

==Solution 4 (answer choices)==
Testing out the box with the center square taking on the value of 5 and 6, we find that they either do not satisfy the first or the second condition. Testing 7, we find that a valid configuration is
<cmath>1 ~8~ 9 </cmath>
<cmath>2 ~ 7 ~6</cmath>
<cmath>3 ~ 4~ 5</cmath>

<imath>\boxed {\textbf{(C) }7}</imath>

~JH. L

==Solution 5==
There are <imath>10</imath> cases of integers <imath>1-9</imath> adding to <imath>18</imath>. Like Solution 1, you realize that all the dark squares are all odd numbers, and the only case with all odd numbers is <imath>1,3,5,9</imath>, meaning that the center square is <imath>\boxed {\textbf{(C) }7}</imath>
